svg.text: The verification block — how it fits the planned workflow
Four tiers, three verification levels, ONE deterministic hard gate. Grounded at tip 0e08ece · research note F8 / F11 / F12 / §4E / §7 items 1 & 5
1 · The workflow schema: every tier asks a question, only one tier can answer it deterministically
FEATURE
roadmap.md
Did the feature deliver the intent the roadmap promised?

eval role, L2 verdict (I03)
different model family, blind to authorship
SOFT · pass^k
one green run is a sample, not a result (F12)
INCREMENT
increments/increment-NN-*.md
Did every slice land, and did they land together?
an aggregation, not a new measurement
AND of the slice gates + the eval verdict
MAST: the objective level is worth +15.6 pp
MIXED
only as strong as its weakest slice gate

## SLICE1: …

2 · The slice ritual: the verify block is a claim, and the harness converts it into evidence
Research §7 item 1 — "contracts become executable". The block stays a plain command list; all discipline lives in code, not in the prompt.
INCREMENT PLAN · increments/increment-NN-*.md
## SLICE2 TESTS: tests/test_x.py (NEW) ```verify …```
GATE 0 · PRE-CHECK — pure code, zero coder tokens
• every referenced path/symbol exists, or is marked NEW
• every CT# is covered by a test on the slice's TESTS: line
• every prescriptive STEP# carries an exit criterion; DEPS: is acyclic
• a ```verify fence outside any ## SLICE section → WARN (grammar-collision trap)
FAIL
→ planner fixes
the plan, not code
PHASE A · BASELINE — before the coder starts, on the untouched tree
Run the slice's verify commands once. Record the exit code per command:
baseline = { cmd → RED | GREEN | ERROR }
PHASE B · FAIL-BEFORE — the non-vacuity filter
Every test file marked NEW must be RED at baseline.
A test that passes before the work is done proves nothing — so it is discarded,
not merely noted. Lint/lint-like commands are exempt: they have no "before".
NEW test already
GREEN → vacuous
→ back to planner
PHASE C · THE CODER IMPLEMENTS
scoped brief = section("SLICE2") — it never sees the rest of the plan. It never writes its own acceptance.
PHASE D · PASS-AFTER — re-run the same commands, same order
Compare per command against the baseline. Not "the suite is green" —
per-command, because attribution is the entire point.
THE TRUTH TABLE ↓
baseline state × after state → verdict. Seven cases, no judgment calls.
Why baseline, not just "green"?
Phoenix (2606.20243): 10 of 11 real repos
have pre-existing test failures.
Without a baseline you cannot tell
which failure is yours — so you
either chase ghosts or learn to
ignore red, which kills the gate.
Why the author writes the test?
VeriMAP (2510.17109): planner-written
verification. AgentCoder (2312.13010):
independent test authorship, 96.3%.
The coder must never write its own
acceptance — that separation is the
strongest guarantee available.
The 34.3% number
patches that passed the functional
tests, 221 violated the acceptance
constraints. Passing tests is not
the same event as being accepted.
3 · The truth table — the whole gate in seven rows
Nothing here is a judgment call, which is why it can live in code instead of a prompt (research F5, §7 item 5).

g.text: WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT ANSWER
Fail-before / pass-after. The slice is real. This is the only PROVEN state.
It passed before anyone worked. It proves nothing about this slice. Agentless discards it.
PRESERVATION held. Nothing broke. Quietly correct — the common case.
Something that worked now fails. PRESERVATION is enforced by construction, not review.
Pre-existing failure, not yours (10 of 11 repos). Recorded, not blocking, never ignored.
You fixed something unasked. Worth an EVIDENCE entry — and a suspicion: was it in scope?
Timeout, missing binary, bad path. "Couldn't run" is not "passed" — a third state.

svg.text: 4 · Two gates, two opposite postures
PRE-CHECK — be forgiving
Judgment calls WARN, never fail: slice count outside 4–7, an orphan verify
fence, a suspiciously thin contract. Re-planning is cheap; a wasted slice run
is not. Too strict here and every deviation costs a turn.
VERIFY GATE — be strict
ERROR is never PASS. A vacuous NEW test is rejected, not tolerated. A
regression blocks. This is the acceptance decision — leniency here is how
the 34.3% false-accept rate gets built, one forgiven red at a time.
Lenient authoring, strict acceptance.
The same tool cannot be both. Splitting the two is what makes the pair usable.
Above the gate, verdicts stay stochastic → pass^k, never one green run (F12).

I02 ADDS — nothing exotic, four small things
1. a runner: commands_for(slice) → three-state result per command
2. a baseline snapshot, stored beside the run (ephemeral, not in the plan)
3. the seven-row comparison, in pure code
4. the fail-before filter on NEW tests
